focus.jnote: The tape flipped risk-on overnight Monday — but today hinges on a single number. The S&P 500 rose 2.35% to close at 7,549.94, marking its largest single-day gain since April 8; the Nasdaq increased 2.74% to close at 25,253.14. The catalyst was oil and geopolitics: hopes for US–Iran diplomacy sent Brent down 5.8% on Monday, and lower oil eased inflation fears, weakened the dollar and lifted risk assets worldwide. Volatility was crushed — the S&P rose 2.35% to 7,550 and the VIX fell 22.31%. The regime is now neutral with the VIX at 19.92, the curve back in contango and SKEW elevated at 150.34; the three-month fell to 20.85. But the overhang is data: October CPI lands today at 8:30am New York time, with consensus at +0.3% headline and +0.2% core. Waller has set the marker: a 0.3% core puts 50bp on the table. Borrowing costs stayed high — the 10-year Treasury yield rose to 4.895%, so the rally is not powered by cheaper money.

The disciplined answer is to sell nothing new today.
